doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ertegun at the Lighthouse live album and the album list
summary: Ertegun came to hear a live recording; Panken lists dates of his Atlantic records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And you were friends with Neshui Ertegun. You’ve said you liked to hang out with him and you liked him.
Was this something that he was encouraging you to do?
No. He didn’t encourage... He came out to the Lighthouse when I did a record there with...I don’t know... But I did a record at the Lighthouse, and Neshui came out for it, and it was a live album...
They probably have it over there, in the cabinet.
Oh, you have all the records here?
We have a lot of them. They didn’t know, but I found them the last time I was here. Do you want me to get them?
According to the album list, Word for Mose is 1964, Mose Allison Alive is 1965, Wild Man On The Loose is ‘65. There’s an album called Down Home Piano. V-8 Ford Blues is ‘66...
I didn’t write that... That was a compilation.
V-8 Ford Blues is a compilation. But Wild Man On The Loose is one of your...
